summary: The quoted/default and direct-output paths are structurally expressible in declarative Swap JSON, but the deployed v1 SwapVM output-first callback (deferred-input settlement) cannot be declared: declarative callback compilers inject the callback script as the whole ABI bytes argument and derive offsets from that argument start, while Aqua embeds the script inside the 22-byte-header packed takerTraitsAndData at a later slice and requires VM patches at limitOffset/floorOffset. The family advertises deferredInput (execution.ts:17-20) and the universal family-dual fixture asserts both the capability and the packed layout. A JSON cutover would either fail that fixture or narrow a verified settlement mode, so no production JSON was authored and the handwritten entry remains authoritative.

existingSource.fact: buildRuntimeLeg advertises settlement {quoteOutput: true, directOutput: true, deferredInput: executor} and accepts deferred-input requests.
deferred input builds runtimeDeferredPayment({tokenOut, executor, debtOffset: 132, ...settlement}) and then embeds its script in takerTraitsAndData.

swap calldata = swap(order,tokenIn,tokenOut,0,takerData(minimum,{recipient?,callbackScript})); the callback is slice 7 inside a 22-byte-header packed taker payload; outgoing offset is takerStart + 22 + ends[6] + 64 and the VM patches outgoing+limitOffset and outgoing+floorOffset; incomingOffset is fixed 356.

takerData packs a 22-byte header with ten cumulative 16-bit slice ends followed by ten slices; slice 7 is the ABI-wrapped callback script. The header flags are 0x61 (direct/default) or 0x45 (output-first callback).

The universal installed-family settlement fixture asserts the exact capability object and the deferred layout: flags 0x45, callback at traits slice 7, incoming 356, script at the ABI-wrapped outgoing offset, and script header 0x0e + input amount.
Existing actual settlement tests construct {kind:'deferred-input', paymentAmount, paymentProgram} and require the leg's deferredInput capability and executor funding account.
aqua-swapvm variant deferred-input is registered as interface/identity/callback/wiring/execution verified, output-first, paymentAccount=executor.

frameworkLimitation.fact: A deferred declaration requires the outer call to have a bytes dataArgument and the incoming callback to have exactly one bytes argument; all other callback args are scalar.

The compiler creates payload = runtimeProgramScript(callback.bytes()), splices payload into args[dataArgument], and computes outgoingOffset as the ABI bytes-argument content start via payloadOffset. This replaces the whole bytes argument; it cannot place the payload inside a packed header/slice table.
The framedSettlement compiler has the same shape: the callback payload must be one bytes argument and its offset is derived from that ABI argument start.

deferredInput is advertised only when definition.deferred or definition.framedSettlement exists. There is no JSON field for a family-provided callback script, nested payload offset, or extra VM patch offsets.

Call declarations have no callback field; the only callback emissions are the deferred/frame compilers above. A plain call to router.swap with a prebuilt takerTraitsAndData would execute the router's callback without the VM authenticating/patching it, so it is not a faithful substitute.
Runtime ABI references are allowed only for scalar uintN/intN/bytes32 leaves, not for a dynamic bytes argument; a nested callback payload cannot be patched at runtime through a plain call.

probe.method: Built the real deployed-v1 swap calldata for a deterministic deferred callback script with aqua codec.takerData, then replicated the declarative compiler's payload splice (declarative-callback.ts:198-201) through encodeDeclarativeCall.

directOutputStaticBytes.meaning: The plain bytes argument path accepts a family-math-produced packed taker payload for direct/default; only the callback script insertion/authentication path is blocked.

probe.runtimeBytesReference: rejected: runtime ABI references require uint256 or bytes32 leaves (full-width int256 also supported)
probe.consequence: A generic-declared deferred execution would send takerTraitsAndData = 0x0e... instead of the 22-byte-header packed payload. The router cannot decode the flags/slices, the callback is not invoked as Aqua expects, and the VM does not patch limit/floor. The family-dual assertions at flags 0x45, slice 7 and incoming 356 would also fail.

whyPartialCutoverIsNotAcceptable: Omitting deferred makes declarativeSettlementCapabilities omit deferredInput (declarative-execution.ts:1023-1024) and fails family-dual-execution.ts:1024, which asserts the complete {quoteOutput,directOutput,deferredInput} object for every installed family.
Declaring the generic deferred compiler compiles but produces non-Aqua calldata (probe above), so historical/output-first settlement and the fixture's layout assertions fail.

The settlement review registry lists deferred-input as verified; narrowing it would require a new not-required/gap classification and would drop an actual production capability, contrary to the family-adaptation requirement to preserve supported settlement modes.
